messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: increment_log_prob plan
parts:
I went with the function-like syntax:

increment_log_prob(e);

The expression e must be assignable to real.

As Marcus suggested, the underlying implementation uses
an accumulator that returns a sum() at the end. Should be
much faster than incremental summations, each of which required
playing with memory and a virtual function call.

The use of lp__ is discouraged by having it print a warning.
The warning indicates that it will go away in the future and
that increment_log_prob() should be used instead.

I replaced all uses of lp__ in the doc and in the example
models with increment_log_prob(). I also replaced all the
mentions of lp__ in the text of the doc.

I added a new section to the doc for increment_log_prob().
I added a small subsection in that section about lp__ mentioning
that it's deprecated.

We could just get rid of it instead of deprecating it,
but I thought this way would be gentler for the users.

Any other suggestions?

- Bob

The thing to do would be to have the code generator recognize
the pattern generated by the parser for this in the abstract
syntax tree. I haven't done any of this kind of simple peephole
optimization yet, but it's definitely possible.

In this case, I'm not too worried about making the thing we're
deprecating more efficient.

The real target should be the transforms at this point, because they
still apply += to lp__ implicitly. And they're not vectorized yet.
We can pass in a reference to the log prob accumulator class instead
of a reference to lp into the contrain() forms of the transforms.

> ? Also, there was an idea that there should be a
>
> |
> reject()
> |
>
> that would just reject the proposal instead of having to do
>
> |
> increment_log_prob(Neg_Infinity());
> |

Thanks for reminding me. I added this to the short-term to-do items.

I'd like to configure it using the Boost error handling so that
it either tosses an exception or does the same thing as incrementing
NaN.

I'd also like to add optional arguments to print as part of the
exception.

I can make this a separate pull request after everything else
settles down. Perhaps after 2.0, depending on how things go.

- Bob
